question_text: Write the chemical equation for the combustion reaction of pentene.

THE EQUATIONS WERE CHECKED ATOM BY ATOM: C₅H₁₀ + 15/2 O₂ → 5CO₂ + 5H₂O has C 5 = 5, H 10 = 10 and O 15 = 10 + 5 = 15; the doubled form 2C₅H₁₀ + 15O₂ → 10CO₂ + 10H₂O has C 10 = 10, H 20 = 20 and O 30 = 20 + 10 = 30. CONTENT CARRIED BEYOND THE PRINTED ANSWER and to be confirmed by a teacher: the doubled whole-number form, and the statement that pent-1-ene and pent-2-ene give the same combustion equation because the molecular formula is the same.

insider_note: Pentene is C₅H₁₀, an alkene — not C₅H₁₂. Write the alkane formula and every coefficient after it comes out wrong.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The formula and the equation
lines: The ending -ene means an alkene, CₙH₂ₙ.
Pentene has five carbon atoms, so it is
Five carbons give 5CO₂ and ten hydrogens
The position of the double bond does not
steps.why: The molecular formula has to be settled before the equation can be balanced, and that is what the -ene ending gives: an alkene has two hydrogen atoms fewer than the alkane with the same carbons. Once C₅H₁₀ is fixed, five carbons give 5CO₂ and ten hydrogens give 5H₂O, which together contain fifteen oxygen atoms.
common_mistakes: Using C₅H₁₂ for pentene. That is pentane, the alkane; pentene is C₅H₁₀.
Writing 6H₂O. Ten hydrogen atoms give five molecules of water.
Expecting the double bond to change the products. Complete combustion gives CO₂ and water.
steps.memory_tip: The ending -ene means CₙH₂ₙ, so five carbons carry ten hydrogens.
steps.margin_note: Write the molecular formula from the -ene ending before balancing anything.

steps.label: The whole-number form
lines: Atoms: 10 C, 20 H and 30 O on each side.
Pent-1-ene and pent-2-ene are both C₅H₁₀,
so both give this same equation.
steps.why: Doubling clears the half molecule of oxygen, and the atom count confirms the result. Because only the molecular formula enters a combustion equation, every pentene gives the same equation whatever the position of its double bond.
common_mistakes: Doubling the oxygen alone and leaving the rest. Every coefficient must be doubled together.
Balancing for a named isomer. Combustion depends on the molecular formula only.
steps.memory_tip: Same molecular formula, same combustion equation, whichever pentene is meant.
steps.margin_note: Give either the fraction form or the doubled form, and check the atom counts.
